test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 08 May 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Cost price of an article is Rs. 350. If the profit percentage is 35 percent, then what is the value of profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit = 35% of **Cost Price (CP)**

Profit = 0.35 × 350

Profit = 35 × 3.5 = 122.5

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 122.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of the article = Rs. 350

**Profit Percentage** = 35%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit Percentage ÷ 100) × **Cost Price (CP)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec5879b9aae0ead26e50c6d277cc251283d004569a10e4bb15d4d971adc4a667.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = (35 ÷ 100) × 350

⇒ Profit = 0.35 × 350

⇒ Profit = (35 × 35) ÷ 10

⇒ Profit = 1225 ÷ 10

⇒ Profit = Rs. 122.5

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 122.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price (SP)

The price at which an article is sold is called its Selling Price. SP = CP + Profit or SP = CP − Loss.

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100. Profit is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.</p
